newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Court to rule on Clabecq future.
newsitem.headline: Court to rule on Clabecq future.

text.p: A Belgian commercial court is due to rule at 1600 hours (1500 GMT) on Friday on the future of loss-making steel maker Forges de Clabecq, Belgian media said on Friday.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy in mid-December after the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc rescue plan by the Walloon Region and after the region - Clabecq's majority shareholder - then withdrew its support for the firm.

But on December 24 the court ruled against declaring Clabecq bankrupt because two experts said the company was still viable and that judging by its order book it could still survive in its current form until the middle of 1997.
The activities of the company, which employs nearly 1,800 people, should be reduced and a restructuring considered thereafter, the experts' report said.

The court then appointed a company receiver to draw up a financial plan based on a full resumption of work from January 6 and the start-up of the furnace from January 4, and said it would give another ruling on January 3 after reading the report.

Belga news agency said three scenarios for Clabecq had been envisaged - continuing activities after declaring bancruptcy, continuing activities without bankruptcy, and carrying on for six months with a debt freeze without declaring bankruptcy.

Clabecq shares, currently suspended, were last quoted at 76 francs on December 19. Bid and ask prices were indicated at seven francs but the actual decline had been limited by a bourse rule capping the movement in cash market shares at 10 percent below or above the previous close.
